title: Lab 2: A debounced button counter
summary: Count button presses on the LEDs. You will meet **bouncing** and fix it with a debouncer and an edge detector.
objectives: Synchronise and debounce an asynchronous input

steps.title: A 4-bit counter
steps.md: Write `counter4.sv`: on every clock with `en = 1` the value increases by one.

steps.title: Try it without debouncing
steps.md: Connect the button directly to `en` (system clock 100 MHz) and press it. Write down what the LEDs do.
steps.hint: The counter runs while the button is held — and jumps by random amounts.

steps.title: Synchronise the button
steps.md: Add a **two flip-flop synchroniser** in front of everything that uses the button.

steps.title: Debounce
steps.md: Accept a new level only after it was stable for **10 ms** (1 000 000 clocks at 100 MHz).

steps.title: Rising-edge detector
steps.md: Make `en` a one-clock pulse when the debounced button goes from 0 to 1.

steps.title: Test on the board
steps.md: Each press must now add exactly **one**. Count 0 → 15 → 0.

questions.text: Why does the counter jump when the button is used directly?
options: The button bounces and `en` is high for millions of clocks
The counter has too few bits

questions.text: Order the blocks from the button pin to the counter.
How many clocks of 100 MHz are 10 ms?
